headline: Generative models enable biomedical counterfactuals in simulation and single-cell data
label: Generative Models For Biomedical Counterfactuals
summary: Counterfactual estimation and agent-level emulation both demand generative or causal models that retain dynamics and adjust for confounders in biomedical data.
synthesis: The shared thread is using learned generative and causal models to answer counterfactual questions in biomedical settings where direct intervention or full simulation is costly. A conditional tabular GAN emulates individual road-injury agents inside a multi-disease agent-based model, reporting an 86.6% run-time reduction while retaining the model's dynamics. SCOUT targets treatment effects, learning a treatment-responsive outcome with two-dimensional confounder adjustment for ATE and CATE estimation in observational biomedical data. A kernel-based regularizer using normalized HSIC is proposed for concept bottleneck generative models to better separate known from unknown factors in single-cell counterfactuals. What is new across these items is the move from covariance-based adjustment toward nonlinear dependence control and agent-level emulation, with counterfactual reasoning as the common target.
